bio.title: Brief Bio
paragraphs: I completed my Ph.D. at Umeå University as a member of the Cooperative and Intelligent Embedded Systems research group. My doctoral work focused on robust, efficient, and scalable cooperative perception systems for autonomous vehicles.

Before pursuing my Ph.D., I spent several years in industry as a machine learning engineer, working on projects involving training computer vision (CV) and natural language processing (NLP) models, as well as model quantization and deployment. (That was a long story from the pre-LLM era.)
The rise of LLMs has changed a lot in the field. These days, my main interests lie in autonomous vehicles, robotics, and efficient inference.
Research interests: autonomous driving; and vision-language-action models for autonomous vehicles; efficient inference.

items.title: Refora
items.tagline: Refora is an AI-native research workspace for Apple Silicon Macs. It brings papers, annotations, evidence maps, notes, and a research agent into one continuous loop—from understanding a passage to tracing a research frontier, developing hypotheses, and turning insight into durable work.
paragraphs: And, of course, this project also owes a little something to Tibo's Codex usage limit reset.

items.title: Cooperative Perception for Next-Generation Autonomous Vehicles
items.description: Develops unified cooperative perception frameworks for realistic multi-agent systems, addressing model heterogeneity, temporal latency, and limited communication bandwidth.

image.alt: Overview connecting the thesis research objectives, four included papers, and their synthesis

items.title: Communication Efficient Cooperative Perception via Codebook-Free Vector Quantization
items.description: A lightweight codebook-free quantization framework that compresses shared BEV features into low-bit integer codes while retaining competitive detection accuracy.

image.alt: Conceptual cooperative perception network connecting a road-side unit and autonomous vehicles

items.title: Towards Model-Agnostic Cooperative Perception
items.venue: International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN), 2025
items.description: Enables intermediate cooperative perception across independently trained, heterogeneous agent models using lightweight feature adaptation and deformable attention.

image.alt: Comparison of single-agent, jointly trained, and model-agnostic cooperative perception

items.title: Latency Robust Cooperative Perception Using Asynchronous Feature Fusion
items.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV), 2025
items.description: Directly fuses asynchronous BEV features and predicts non-discrete scene flow from cached history to remain robust under communication latency.

image.alt: Cooperative detection under 300 millisecond latency, with and without LRCP compensation

items.title: InputMix: A Strategy to Regularize and Balance Multi-Modality and Multi-View Model Learning
items.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP), 2024
items.description: Regularizes multi-input networks and balances modality or view contributions by mixing input pairs and training against weighted soft targets.

image.alt: Attribution maps comparing baseline fusion with InputMix on RGB and depth inputs

items.title: An Online Semi-Supervised P300 Speller Based on Extreme Learning Machine
items.description: An online self-training P300 speller that uses a regularized weighted sequential extreme learning machine to reduce calibration time and computational cost while maintaining spelling accuracy.
items.authors: Junjie Wang, Zhenghui Gu, Zhuliang Yu, Yuanqing Li

image.alt: Graphical user interface of the in-house P300 speller
